intended_object: For a morphism f : X ⟶ Y in a Frobenius exact category, the short sequence Y ⟶ cone(f) ⟶ ΣX. Here cone(f) is the pushout of the chosen inflation X ⟶ I(X) along -f, and the sequence is the cobase change of the chosen conflation X ⟶ I(X) ⟶ ΣX, i.e. the tail of Happel's standard triangle. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body packages pushout.inr : Y ⟶ pushout(i(X), -f) and the map out of the pushout induced by the chosen deflation I(X) ⟶ ΣX and by 0 on Y into a ShortComplex; the zero-composite proof is inr_desc. This is exactly the cobase change of the chosen suspension conflation along the pushout square. The next theorem in the file, conflation_coneSequence, checks that it equals cobaseChange S sq and is a conflation, as the docstring says. The -f sign is a convention that makes the cone conflation read X ⟶ I(X) ⊞ Y ⟶ cone f, and it does not change the cone up to isomorphism. The setting (a Frobenius exact structure on a preadditive category with a zero object and biproducts) is the natural one for this construction, since it relies on the chosen projective-injective presentations. Mathlib's triangulated-category library builds mapping cones from chain complexes, not from Frobenius exact categories, so it offers no counterpart.
